statement: Let n = len(nums). For an index i with 0 <= i <= n-2, define L(i) = nums[0] * nums[1] * ... * nums[i] and R(i) = nums[i+1] * ... * nums[n-1] as mathematical integer products. Whenever the function returns a result r, the following holds: if there exists i with 0 <= i <= n-2 and gcd(L(i), R(i)) = 1, then r is the least such i (0 <= r <= n-2, gcd(L(r), R(r)) = 1, and for every j with 0 <= j < r, gcd(L(j), R(j)) > 1); if no such i exists, then r = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 1 <= n <= 10^4 and, for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= nums[k] <= 10^6.

statement: The function returns a result r for every input satisfying the preconditions; it does not fail, overflow, or access an out-of-bounds index.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 1 <= n <= 10^4 and, for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= nums[k] <= 10^6.

statement: Let n = len(nums). Whenever the function returns a result r, either r = -1 or 0 <= r <= n-2. Equivalently, -1 <= r <= n-2.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 1 <= n <= 10^4 and, for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= nums[k] <= 10^6.

statement: Let n = len(nums). For 0 <= i <= n-2 let L(i) and R(i) be the mathematical products of nums[0..i] and nums[i+1..n-1]. Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, the split at r is valid: 0 <= r <= n-2 and gcd(L(r), R(r)) = 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 1 <= n <= 10^4 and, for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= nums[k] <= 10^6.

statement: Let n = len(nums). For 0 <= i <= n-2 let L(i) and R(i) be the mathematical products of nums[0..i] and nums[i+1..n-1]. Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, every earlier split is invalid: for every j with 0 <= j < r, gcd(L(j), R(j)) > 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 1 <= n <= 10^4 and, for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= nums[k] <= 10^6.

statement: Let n = len(nums). For 0 <= i <= n-2 let L(i) and R(i) be the mathematical products of nums[0..i] and nums[i+1..n-1]. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = -1 if and only if there is no index i with 0 <= i <= n-2 and gcd(L(i), R(i)) = 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 1 <= n <= 10^4 and, for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= nums[k] <= 10^6.

statement: Let n = len(nums). For 0 <= i <= n-2 let L(i) and R(i) be the mathematical products of nums[0..i] and nums[i+1..n-1]. Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exists a valid split i (that is, 0 <= i <= n-2 and gcd(L(i), R(i)) = 1), then r != -1 and r <= i for every such valid split i.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 1 <= n <= 10^4 and, for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= nums[k] <= 10^6.

statement: Let n = len(nums). Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, every element on the left of the split is coprime to every element on the right: for every a with 0 <= a <= r and every b with r < b < n, gcd(nums[a], nums[b]) = 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 1 <= n <= 10^4 and, for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= nums[k] <= 10^6.

statement: Let n = len(nums). Whenever the function returns a result r = -1, every split fails: for every i with 0 <= i <= n-2 there exist indices a and b with 0 <= a <= i < b < n and gcd(nums[a], nums[b]) > 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 1 <= n <= 10^4 and, for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= nums[k] <= 10^6.

statement: Whenever find_valid_split(nums) returns a result r and find_valid_split(nums') returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 1 <= n <= 10^4 and, for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= nums[k] <= 10^6. Let nums' be any slice such that len(nums') = n and, for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= nums'[k] <= 10^6 and nums'[k] has exactly the same set of prime divisors as nums[k].
